I’m ready to provide brand assets, product data, and copy as soon as we kick off, and I’m happy to work in milestones—design approval, theme build, catalogue import, then final QA—so you’re never waiting on feedback. item.title: Donations SaaS MVP Build
item.description:
5000-10000 GBP | I’m ready to commission the first production-ready release of Taleevo, a multi-tenant donations and engagement platform for UK churches and charities. The goal is to take the project from architecture to deployment on AWS, handing me a fully documented codebase and live environment that my team will own outright.
Scope of the MVP • Donation flow: day-one support for NFC tap donations only (QR journeys can remain stubbed for future sprints). • Payments: Stripe Connect integration covering one-off, weekly and monthly recurring gifts, plus donor-selectable funds and full reconciliation logic. • Gift Aid: capture declarations and surface them in finance reports—no need to generate HMRC files or handle direct submission at this stage. • Multi-tenancy: each church or charity sits in its own tenant, with role-based access limited to administrators and finance staff. • Core admin: dashboards, user management, fund setup, basic reporting. • Security & DevOps: infrastructure as code, CI/CD, GDPR-compliant data handling and a documented AWS deployment playbook.
What I need from you 1. Evidence of similar payment or SaaS products you’ve shipped. 2. Your proposed tech stack (I’m open, though TypeScript/Node, React, PostgreSQL and AWS serverless are attractive). 3. A high-level delivery plan with milestones, timeline and fixed-price quote. 4. Post-launch support terms.
Acceptance criteria • All features above implemented, passing agreed test cases. • Source code, IaC scripts and AWS accounts transferred to my organisation. • Clean README and developer hand-over documentation. • Successful end-to-end test: donor taps NFC tag, completes Stripe payment, Gift Aid declaration is stored, finance report reflects transaction in the correct tenant.
If this fits your expertise, let’s discuss your approach and firm up scope quickly so we can move into build.

item.title: Magazine Production & Digital Operations VA
item.description:
5-10 GBP/hr | # Magazine Production & Digital Operations VA | WordPress, Facebook & AI
**Remote | 10–15 hours per week initially | Potential 40 hours per week from January 2027**
### About the Opportunity
We're launching **Around Ashford**, a brand-new UK local publishing and digital media business, on **1st December 2026**.
Our business includes six bi-monthly local magazines, an online business directory, community events, local advertising and plans for national franchise expansion.
Our website is almost ready, and we're looking for an exceptional VA to join us before launch, learn our systems and help us grow.
**This is a long-term opportunity, not a collection of occasional freelance tasks.**
### Your Responsibilities
**Magazine Production** - Produce professional magazine layouts ready for commercial printing. - Prepare print-ready PDFs, including CMYK, bleed, crop marks and correct resolution. - Manage advertising artwork, production deadlines and printer communication. - Coordinate production across six magazine editions.
**Facebook Marketing** - Create compelling, scroll-stopping Facebook posts. - Design graphics using Canva and AI. - Schedule regular posts to build awareness before and after launch. - Promote businesses, events and advertising opportunities. - Help grow our audience and generate enquiries.
**Email Marketing** - Write engaging, persuasive emails. - Schedule campaigns using Brevo. - Manage contact tagging, segmentation and email lists. - Create automated follow-up sequences and newsletters. - Track enquiries and responses.
**WordPress & Business Operations** - Learn and manage our new WordPress backend. - Maintain directory listings, events, jobs and advertiser accounts. - Manage customer enquiries, bookings and renewals. - Coordinate day-to-day administration and suppliers. - Find opportunities to improve efficiency using AI and automation.
### Communication Is Extremely Important
You MUST speak excellent, fluent English and be confident speaking with UK customers and suppliers by telephone or Zoom.
You must also have:
- Professional-quality headset and microphone. - Excellent audio quality without background noise. - Fast, reliable and secure internet. - Backup internet and power arrangements. - Secure computer and quiet working environment. - Availability during agreed UK working hours.
### The Person We're Looking For
Our founder is a fast-moving entrepreneur who values speed, initiative and results.
**We want facts, not lengthy explanations.**
When asked a question, give a clear, concise answer. We don't need a chapter explaining how you intend to complete a task.
You should be:
- Highly proactive and self-motivated. - Extremely organised and dependable. - Quick to learn new systems. - Confident making sensible decisions independently. - Comfortable using ChatGPT and AI daily. - Commercially aware and interested in business growth. - Able to work quickly without sacrificing quality.
**Previous experience producing magazines for commercial printers is essential.**
### Hours & Growth
**November 2026:** 10–15 hours weekly, learning our systems and preparing for launch.
**1st December 2026:** Official launch.
**January 2027 onwards:** Potential to increase towards 40 hours weekly as the business gains momentum.
Facebook marketing will be central to generating awareness and attracting customers.
The faster we grow our audience, acquire advertisers and generate revenue, the sooner we expect to increase working hours.
We want someone who is motivated to help make that happen!
### How to Apply
Please include:
1. Examples of magazines you have personally produced for commercial printing. 2. A 60–90 second video introducing yourself in English. 3. Your experience with WordPress, Facebook, Canva, Brevo and ChatGPT. 4. Details of your headset, internet connection and backup arrangements. 5. Your hourly rate and availability for UK working hours.
**Applications without evidence of magazine production experience will not be considered.**
We're looking for one outstanding person who wants to grow with our business and become a trusted, long-term member of our team.

item.title: Senior Magento 2 Developer — Ongoing Part-Time Contract
item.description:
10-15 GBP/hr | Remote worldwide | Initially 15–20 hours per week | Rate negotiable based on demonstrated Magento expertise
We are an established UK ecommerce business seeking a hands-on senior Magento 2 developer for a long-term working relationship. You will work directly with the business owner to maintain and improve an existing store, investigate technical problems and deliver carefully scoped projects. Candidates worldwide are welcome, with agreed UK working-hour overlap.
The role starts part-time, with potential to grow towards full-time as the workload and working relationship develop. Increased hours are not guaranteed.
THE WORK - Assess, install and update third-party extensions, resolve compatibility issues and test their effect on existing functionality. - Investigate checkout, payment, shipping and tax issues. - Improve performance, including database queries, caching and frontend behaviour. - Develop and maintain custom modules, inventory workflows, imports and API integrations. - Make practical frontend improvements within an existing theme. - Maintain clear estimates, source control, release notes, test evidence and rollback procedures.
TECHNICAL EXPERIENCE Our platform is Magento Open Source 2.4.x with approximately 25,000 SKUs, an established Luma/Porto-based frontend and multiple third-party extensions. Experience maintaining a catalogue of this scale is important.
You should have: - Substantial hands-on Magento 2 experience, ideally five or more years, including ongoing ownership of live stores. - Strong PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, Knockout.js, RequireJS, HTML and CSS skills. - Practical understanding of Magento MSI, reservations, salable quantity, indexing, cron and queues. - Experience diagnosing Redis/Varnish caching and performance issues. - Confidence with Composer, Git, Linux, staging environments and controlled deployments. - Experience creating maintainable Magento modules and working with REST APIs and data imports. - Clear written and spoken English and the ability to explain technical trade-offs to a business owner.
Adobe/Magento certification is welcome, but demonstrated delivery and sound judgement matter most.
WORKING ARRANGEMENT We expect to begin with a small paid technical trial on staging, with scope and an hours cap agreed in advance. A successful trial would lead to an initial 6–8-week part-time engagement, reviewed together before extending.
Please propose regular availability and at least two hours of overlap with UK business hours on agreed working days. Release support and any out-of-hours work will be agreed separately; this is not a 24/7 on-call role.
Work will follow a prioritised backlog. Estimates and additional scope must be agreed before work starts. Production changes require approval, appropriate testing and a rollback plan. Code and technical documentation must be maintained in the client's repository.
We prefer to work directly with the developer doing the work. Please disclose any agency arrangement or proposed subcontracting in your application.
TO APPLY Please provide concise answers: 1. Describe two Magento 2 stores or projects you have personally maintained, your responsibilities and one difficult problem you solved. Anonymised examples are welcome where client confidentiality applies. 2. Describe an extension conflict, checkout fault or caching issue you diagnosed. How did you find the cause and verify the fix? 3. How would you test shared inventory across different product SKUs, including simultaneous orders, cancellations and refunds? A short explanation is sufficient; no unpaid implementation is requested. 4. Explain your normal staging, source-control, testing, deployment and rollback workflow. 5. State your best hourly rate and your proposed monthly price for a regular 20-hour working week. Specify included monthly hours, any minimum commitment and the rate for additional agreed hours. Give your weekly availability, UK working-hour overlap and earliest start date. Include any relevant certification and a code sample you have permission to share, if available.
Company details will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates. Please apply through this platform.

item.title: Secure Multi-Tenant AI Video Editing, Distribution, and Project Manager Platform
item.description:
250-750 USD | Title: Senior engineer (Claude Code + security) to turn our AI video-editing factory into a secure, multi-client product
About us We’re a media distribution brand that makes a lot of short vertical video ads for TikTok and Instagram. Over the last few months we built an in-house AI “creative factory” with Claude Code. It does the work of a video editor: it picks up tasks from our project board and edits the raw creator footage into a finished ad. A human reviews and approves, and only then is the final file rendered and delivered.
It works, but it’s a prototype: it runs on one Mac, the keys sit in a .env file, and it’s built for one company. We want an engineer to make it professional, secure and repeatable so it can run for several businesses, each with its own brand, accounts and data.
What exists today
Pipeline: Node 22 server with SQLite. Stations are Intake → Edit → QA → Human review → Render → Delivery. A live “factory floor” web UI shows the jobs moving between stations. Workers: Python plus ffmpeg. Editor: each ad is an editable timeline project in an open-source web video editor (a customised OpenFilm Studio). The reviewer can open each timeline, change it and approve it. Integrations: the Asana API (task pickup, custom fields), the Frame.io V4 API (delivery) and Google Drive (footage). Guardrails: Claude Code hooks, subagents and skills, plus spend caps per day and per job.
What we want built
A cloud deployment. Everything runs on a server: footage never touches a laptop, and nothing is rendered until a human approves. A desktop workstation app for Mac. It’s a thin client: several jobs open at once, each in its own timeline window, all streamed from the cloud. Multi-tenancy. Each business gets its own isolated workspace: data, footage, brand kit, API connections, spend limits and users. Repeatable onboarding. Adding a new business should be config, not code: connect Asana, Drive and Frame.io, upload brand assets, set the rules. Production quality: CI, tests, monitoring, logs, backups and documentation.
Must-haves
Strong, hands-on Claude Code experience: CLAUDE.md, subagents, skills, hooks, MCP servers, and ideally the Claude Agent SDK and headless runs. Please show real examples. Cybersecurity, applied. We will test you on: secrets management and least-privilege service accounts tenant isolation (one client can never see another client’s footage or keys) zero-trust access to internal tools (no exposed admin ports) webhook signature checks prompt-injection defence: our agents read task text, scripts and comments, which are untrusted input supply-chain hygiene (pinned dependencies) and audit logs Node.js and Python in production, Linux servers, ffmpeg or other media-pipeline experience. Clear written English and async communication.
Nice to have
Swift or desktop-app experience (Tauri or native macOS) Experience with video at scale (proxies, streaming, GPU or headless rendering) Hetzner, Modal, AWS, or Cloudflare (Access/Tunnel) SOC 2-style thinking: access reviews, data retention, incident response
How to apply (answers without these will be skipped)
Start your bid with the word “VSRL”. Describe a Claude Code hook, subagent or MCP server you’ve built, and what it did. In 3–5 sentences: how would you stop an AI agent from following instructions hidden in a client’s task description? How would you isolate tenants’ files and API keys on a shared server? Links to relevant work (GitHub, case studies).
Budget: $300 / Month (negotiable) · Longterm job - at least for the next 6 months. We’ll share the full architecture under an NDA after an interview. Contract under USA cybersecurity and copyright laws.

A User could have no account as like outbid.lol if he only to post a ranked listing. if the user wants to post unranked listings or both, he needs to have an account. 2. How the ranking system should work
Based on the actual Outbid.lol model, the central mechanic is: A person submits their website, product, or social media profile. They choose how much they want to pay. Higher payments receive higher positions (an increment must be met for a higher position). Anyone can submit a higher bid to climb the leaderboard. If someone increases their own bid, they only pay the difference. Once payment is confirmed, the leaderboard updates automatically. With more higher bidding, the lowered previous bidding will be kept to lower position in order, for example, with 2 higher biddings added on, the initial 10th bidding will be moved down to 12th position, always above unranked listings
For example: Rank Product Total bid #1 Product A $500 #2 Product B $300 #3 Product C $150 #4 Product D $50
If someone bids $550 (suppose the minimum increment is $50), they become #1. Equal bids should be ordered by who paid first. This follows the core ranking model described by Outbid.lol.
If the minimum increment is $20, a user bids $320 will get his listing the #2 position.
A difference from outbid.lol: A poster can submit an unranked listing at a plain fee, for example $10 per month, or at a discounted fee: $100 for a year, and this fee is nonrefundable. Unranked listing can’t be upgraded to ranked listing
4. Recommended technology I'd recommend this stack for a scalable first version: Component Technology Frontend Next.js Design Tailwind CSS Database Supabase / PostgreSQL Authentication Supabase Auth Payments Stripe or another supported payment provider, or use payment processor such as dodopayments.com
Hosting Vercel AI features OpenAI API
Important backend features: Automatic ranking calculations. Secure payment verification through webhooks. Duplicate listing detection. User account management. Bid and payment history. Admin dashboard and moderation. Important: Never update a ranking just because the user clicked Pay. Only update it after verified payment confirmation.
5. Design direction I'd suggest a modern dark interface with: Black or charcoal background. Purple/blue accent colors. Large #1 leaderboard spotlight. Clear bid amounts. Green claim buttons. Live ranking updates. Responsive mobile layout.
How should people claim a ranked position? 1. Ranking / claiming method Paid bidding — users pay to claim or outbid positions, like Outbid.lol. Free claiming — users claim available positions without paying. Both — free listings with paid upgrades to higher positions.
2. What can people post? Websites, products, and AI tools Anything — users create their own lists and rankings People, profiles, and social media accounts Custom categories and user-created leaderboards
